region: Industry City, Sunset Park · Brooklyn, New York
about: Fort Hamilton Distillery began with rye. When bartender Alex Clark and his wife, Amy Grindeland, founded the company in 2016, Clark wanted the whiskey behind the original Manhattan and Old Fashioned. In the eighteenth century the Northeast was the center of American rye production, and Prohibition all but wiped the style out of New York City. The distillery is named for Brooklyn’s Fort Hamilton and runs a bar and tasting room in Industry City, Sunset Park.

Double Barrel is the cocktail-minded companion to the flagship single barrel rye. It blends three straight ryes: Fort Hamilton’s own, one distilled at Taconic Distillery in Stanfordville from 100% New York-grown grain (90% rye, 10% malted barley), and one from MGP in Indiana (95% rye, 5% malted barley). The whiskeys age in 30- and 53-gallon barrels at a number 3 char and are bottled at 92 proof without chill filtration.

The distillery describes an herbal nose of dill, fennel and walnut skin, then dark cocoa, caramel-covered pretzel and yellow apple with honey, ending on a touch of sea salt. Clark priced and proofed it for the bar: rye was the original whiskey of the Manhattan and the Sazerac, and at 92 proof this one keeps its spice and backbone under vermouth, bitters and ice.
